title: Paramartha Guru Tale 54

full_text:
Guru Paramartha was preparing for the festival of Deepavali, the festival of lights. The ashram possessed an ancient, ornate seven-tiered brass standing lamp, designed to hold forty-nine oil wicks.

Matti was sent to the storehouse to fetch five bottles of sesame oil to fill the lamp.

Returning with empty hands, Matti wept: 'Alas, Master! The storehouse is empty; the rats tipped over the oil jars, and not a single drop of sesame oil remains in the ashram!'

The Guru was distressed: 'A festival of lights without a lamp is an inauspicious catastrophe! What other liquids do we possess?'

Peedan reported: 'The dairy farmer has just delivered four large pails of rich, fresh, unpasteurized buffalo milk!'

Madayan immediately formulated his Sacred Dairy Combustion Theory: 'Why do we burn base vegetable oils in the presence of the gods? Milk is the sacred essence of the cow! Butter originates from milk; ghee originates from butter; therefore, milk possesses the latent, concentrated fire of pure ghee! If we fill the brass lamp with fresh buffalo milk, it will burn with a pure, white, heavenly, celestial flame that smells of sandalwood!'

The Guru was enraptured: 'A sublime theological discovery! Fill the forty-nine reservoirs with buffalo milk!'

The disciples filled all forty-nine tiers of the brass lamp to the brim with rich, white buffalo milk. They soaked cotton wicks in the milk, placed them in the spouts, and prepared to light them.

Guru Paramartha took a flaming match and applied it to the first wick.

The match hissed against the cold, wet milk and went out.

He struck a second match; it sputtered and died.

Madayan intervened: 'The milk requires pre-heating! Bring the kitchen blowpipe and fan the embers!'

The disciples blew on the wicks with bamboo blowpipes, holding burning camphor blocks against the wet cotton.

After ten minutes of frantic blowing, the wicks did not ignite with a white celestial flame; instead, the milk in the brass bowls began to curdle, scorch, and burn against the hot metal!

A thick, acrid, suffocating cloud of black smoke billowed through the temple hall, carrying the foul, sickening stench of burnt milk, scorched cheese, and charred cotton!

The disciples began coughing and choking: 'COUGH! COUGH! MY EYES! IT SMELLS LIKE A BURNING DAIRY!'

Guru Paramartha fled into the courtyard, coughing violently, his white robes stained with black soot.

The temple priest who had arrived for the ceremony stopped at the gate, sniffing the air in horror: 'What abomination are you burning? Has a cow caught fire in your sanctuary?'

Wiping soot from his tears, Guru Paramartha declared: 'The buffalo milk was spiritually impure; it had not undergone the necessary meditation to release its latent fire!'

The priest brought two bottles of cheap sesame oil, lit the lamps, and the festival proceeded, while the disciples scrubbed scorched cheese from the brass lamp till midnight.
moral: Feeding butterfat to a lamp wick produces foul smoke instead of holy illumination.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
